keyframe_review.note: 47.0 km2 (a five-vertex rectangle, 12.55-12.63 E, 43.73-43.80 N) for 1797..1798 against 61.19 km2 in the San Marino infobox, a ratio of 0.77: within a factor of two. The shape is not on San Marino: the seed gives its modern country as Italy, and the gazetteer resolves it to one cell at 12.53 E 43.79 N against the country's one cell at 12.41 E 43.91 N, with no cell in common; its nearest corner (12.55 E, 43.80 N) lies about 18 km south-east of Monte Titano (12.4578 E, 43.9424 N) and its centroid about 22 km. The correction {country: San Marino} moves it onto the state. Napoleon's offer 'to extend its territory according to its needs' was 'politely declined by San Marino', so the territory stays the 1463 one.

keyframe_review.note: Identical to the 1797 shape (47.0 km2) and displaced the same way (no cell in common with San Marino). The 1815 Congress of Vienna 'ratified San Marino's independence in 1815'; nothing on the pages changes the territory in 1799.

region.text: Monte Titano and the first community

ledger.note: 301: San Marino is founded. 'According to legend, San Marino was founded in 301 AD.' The page gives no month; the legend is the only date. Territory before 1463 was Monte Titano (the page also dates Chiesanuova to 1320).

wars.name: Napoleon's Italian campaign and San Marino (1797)
wars.outcome: No fighting: the advance of Napoleon's army in 1797 'presented a brief threat to the independence of San Marino'; the regent Antonio Onofri won Napoleon's respect, Napoleon promised 'to guarantee and protect the independence of the Republic' and offered to extend its territory, which the regents declined; the state was 'recognized by Napoleon by the Treaty of Tolentino, in 1797'.
wars.note: Months are not on the pages except Berthier's letter of 5 February 1797. No territory moved.

certainty.note: Monte Titano and the early community; the pages date only Chiesanuova (1320).
'Since then, the size of San Marino has remained unchanged' (History of San Marino, after the 1463 grants); the 1739-40 occupation by the legate of Ravenna did not change the borders.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Republic of San Marino' row covers only 1797..1799 (two identical 47 km2 shapes), but the state did not end in 1799: it runs from the legendary foundation of 301 to today. The full-life dossier already exists as san-marino.json (cliopatria_names [], written by an additions batch). This dossier exists because the two Cliopatria shapes of slug republic-of-san-marino need a reviewing dossier; it keeps the same identity and carries only the Napoleonic window (keyframes 1797..1799). Recommended: merge, listing 'Republic of San Marino' in san-marino.json's cliopatria_names and reviewing the two shapes there, and drop this file (or the colour agent will give one state two colours). Nothing on the pages changed the territory in 1797-1799: Napoleon offered to extend it and the regents declined; the Papal States border it in 1797..1798, the Cisalpine Republic in 1797..1799 and the Revolutionary Roman Republic in 1799 (Cliopatria seed), none with a border change recorded. The Congress of Vienna ratified independence in 1815 (History page). The History page gives no month for the foundation, so none is recorded (san-marino.json uses September). Review repair 2026-11-01: the shapes are drawn about 18 km south-east of Monte Titano (no cell shared with the country), which the corrections fix; the merge into san-marino.json (cliopatria_names, these two keyframe reviews, deletion of this file) is the orchestrator's, because san-marino.json is outside this batch.
